G=(V,E)G=(V,E)G=(V,E): graph → directed graph / undirected graph (symmetric). For undirected graph, degree of a node (kik_iki​): # of edges adjacent to node iii.

For directed graph:

Total degree of node iii: ki=kiin+kioutk_i=k_i^{\mathrm{in}}+k_i^{\mathrm{out}}ki​=kiin​+kiout​. Average degree: kin‾=kout‾=∣E∣/N\overline{k^{\mathrm{in}}}=\overline{k^{\mathrm{out}}}=|E|/Nkin=kout=∣E∣/N. Induced subgraph: a subset of the vertices of the graph and all of the edges connecting pairs of vertices in that subset. Ego-network of a target node: an induced subgraph which is induced by its target node and its direct neighbors. Complete graph: an undirected graph with ∣E∣max⁡|E|_{\max}∣E∣max​ edges.

∣E∣max⁡=(N2)=N(N−1)2,Average degree=N−1.|E|_{\max}=\binom N2=\frac{N(N-1)}2,\qquad\text{Average degree}=N-1.∣E∣max​=(2N​)=2N(N−1)​,Average degree=N−1.

Clique: a subset of vertices of an undirected graph such that every two distinct vertices in the clique are adjacent. ⇒ Its induced subgraph is complete. Maximal clique: a clique that cannot be extended by including one more adjacent vertex. (It is not a subset of a larger clique.) Bipartite graph: a graph whose nodes can be divided into two disjoint sets UUU and VVV s.t. every edge connects a node in UUU and one in VVV.

Note. Sparse graph: ∣E∣≪∣E∣max⁡|E|\ll|E|_{\max}∣E∣≪∣E∣max​. Directed: N(N−1)N(N-1)N(N−1) / undirected: (N2)\binom N2(2N​). Edge lists / adjacency lists

Connectivity

Connectivity of undirected graph: if every pair of vertices in the graph is connected, i.e. there is a path between every pair of vertices. Connected component: an induced subgraph in which any two vertices are connected, and which is connected to no additional vertices in the rest of the graph. Directed graph: strongly connected if every vertex is reachable from every other vertex. Strongly connected components form a partition. Clustering coefficient of node AAA: the probability that two randomly selected friends of AAA are friends with each other. Bridge (A,B)(A,B)(A,B) if deleting the edge causes AAA and BBB to be in different components. Local bridge if AAA and BBB have no common friend. But there should exist some path A→BA\to BA→B. Span of a local bridge (A,B)(A,B)(A,B): distance of AAA to BBB if the local bridge (A,B)(A,B)(A,B) is removed.

Ch. 2 Centrality Measures

How can we define the importance?

① Degree centrality

#\## of adjacent nodes.

② Betweenness centrality

Compute all-pairs shortest-paths in a graph. (모든 쌍 최단 경로 문제 ⇒ Floyd–Warshall algorithm) ← 찾아보기!! Node betweenness: # of times a node lies on the shortest path between other nodes. ⇒ Shows which nodes are bridges between nodes in a network. Edge betweenness: # of shortest paths passing through the edge. ⇒ Bridges and local bridges have high betweenness.

③ Closeness centrality

Average length of the shortest path between the node and all other nodes in the graph. ← node's.

④ Hubs & Authorities

Idea: Receiving many links → receiving collective endorsement (보증). ⇒ If there is a link from ppp to qqq, then ppp confers authority on qqq. We desire pages (relevant and authoritative, voting by in-links). Ex. query: “newspaper” (newspaper 검색했을 때 무슨 페이지에 자료들이 어떻게 나오려나…) Let SSS be the set of web pages returned to be relevant. 간단한 버전:

  1. Extract the subgraph induced by SSS and its neighbors.
  2. Count in-links to pages as authority score.
  3. Hub score = out-link의 authority score 합.
  4. New authority score = ∑hub\sum\mathrm{hub}∑hub.

Authority score: the sum of incoming weights. (Initial = 1.) Hub score: the sum of authority scores that the page points to. Normalization: we only care about relative sizes.

Two issues with PageRank

  1. Dangling nodes (no out-links).
  2. Sinks.

Solution: add links to all nodes in the graph from every node.

Random walks (Random Surfer Model)

Web surfer starts at a random page. With probability α\alphaα, he follows out-links with equal probability, and with 1−α1-\alpha1−α, he jumps to a random page. Stationary distribution is the probability of landing at pages.

Power method

Initialize xxx as 1−αne\dfrac{1-\alpha}{n}en1−α​e. For each node vvv: Repeat criteria: ① predefined max reached, ② ∥x(k+1)−x(k)∥∞<ε\|x^{(k+1)}-x^{(k)}\|_\infty<\varepsilon∥x(k+1)−x(k)∥∞​<ε ← predefined tolerance.

Data-driven PageRank

Focus subset of nodes need to be updated. (worklist)

  1. Initialize worklist as the entire vertex set.
  2. Pick a node from the worklist (pop), and compute its PageRank. If updated, all its outgoing nbrs are added to worklist. If difference <ε<\varepsilon<ε, do not update.
  3. Repeat until worklist becomes empty.
  4. Normalize so that sum = 1.

Ch. 4 Graph Clustering

Girvan–Newman algorithm

Intuition: high betweenness edges tend to connect nodes far from each other, i.e. they tend to be local bridges between clusters.

  1. Compute betweenness for all edges.
  2. Remove the edge whose betweenness is the highest.
  3. Continue until no edges left or stopping criteria.

Modularity optimization

Where AijA_{ij}Aij​: weight of the edge between iii and jjj.

ki=∑jAij,ci:community to which i is assigned,k_i=\sum_jA_{ij},\quad c_i:\text{community to which }i\text{ is assigned},ki​=j∑​Aij​,ci​:community to which i is assigned,

Random configuration model

Cut each edge into two halves (each half-edge: stub). Rewire randomly with same degree distribution but uniformly random connections. Expected # of edges between iii and jjj of degrees kik_iki​ and kjk_jkj​:

ki⋅kj2m=kikj2m.k_i\cdot\frac{k_j}{2m}=\frac{k_ik_j}{2m}.ki​⋅2mkj​​=2mki​kj​​.

If Q>0.3Q>0.3Q>0.3, then partition is regarded to have a significant community structure. ⇒ Modularity can be used as metric that measures the quality of community structure. We can identify communities by maximizing modularity.

Louvain method

Greedy algorithm that optimizes modularity. Assign a different community to each node.

  1. For each node iii, iii의 neighbor jjj에 대해서 iii를 jjj의 community로 옮겼을 때 얻는 modularity 계산 → 가장 최대가 되는 곳으로 iii 이동 (gain >0>0>0). If no positive gain, iii는 그대로… Local maxima of modularity를 얻으면 이 과정 반복 멈춤.
  2. Build a new network whose nodes are the communities found in the first phase. (Community 자체를 하나의 node로 취급.) 다시 phase 1 적용.

Consider a random walk that traversed (t,v)(t,v)(t,v) and now in vvv. The next step:

  1. Going back to ttt.
  2. Go another direct neighbor of ttt.
  3. Go further from ttt.

α\alphaα: search bias. ① ppp: return parameter.

  • p↑p\uparrowp↑: avoids 2-hop redundancy.
  • p↓p\downarrowp↓: keep the walk local close to starting node.

② Walk: (t,v)→(v,x)(t,v)\to(v,x)(t,v)→(v,x), xxx is a direct neighbor of ttt. 홉이동의 probability 합이 1이어야 해서 여기서는 parameter 설정 ×. ③ qqq: walk-away parameter.

  • q>1q>1q>1: walk is biased towards nodes close to node ttt.
  • q<1q<1q<1: visit nodes which are further away from node ttt.

Given walk (t,v)(t,v)(t,v), we consider the next step in terms of ttt. (t,v)→(v,x)(t,v)\to(v,x)(t,v)→(v,x), and xxx is interpreted in terms of ttt. 2nd order random walk with two parameters ppp & qqq. BFS-like walk: low ppp. DFS-like walk: low qqq.

node2vec algorithm

  1. Compute the random walk transition probabilities.
  2. Simulate rrr random walks of length ℓ\ellℓ starting from each node uuu.
  3. Optimize using stochastic gradient descent.

L=∑u∈V∑v∈NR(u)−log⁡P(v∣zu).L=\sum_{u\in V}\sum_{v\in N_R(u)}-\log P(v|z_u).L=u∈V∑​v∈NR​(u)∑​−logP(v∣zu​).

Multi-label classification

  • Spectral clustering: take top ddd eigenvectors of the normalized Laplacian matrix of the given graph.
  • DeepWalk: simulating uniform random walks.
  • LINE: to learn ddd-dim feature vector, learn d/2d/2d/2-dim by BFS-style simulation and learn next d/2d/2d/2-dim by sampling nodes at a 2-hop distant nodes.

We should train a classifier using learned features.

Summary of node2vec

Define a random walk that can trade off between BFS & DFS. p,qp,qp,q parameter로 BFS와 DFS를 조절.

Dropout

During training, a unit is present with probability ppp and is connected to units in the next layer with weight www. During testing, unit is always present and weights are multiplied by ppp. GNN에서는 message function에 적용.

Layer connectivity

How to connect the GNN layers. Stack GNN layers sequentially. Input: node feature xvx_vxv​. Output: node embedding hv(L)h_v^{(L)}hv(L)​. ⇒ Over-smoothing problem: all node embedding vectors converge to same vector. 우리는 노드마다 다른 임베딩을 원함. Respective field of a GNN The set of nodes that determine the embedding of a node of interest. In a kkk-layer GNN, each node has respective field of kkk-hop distant nbrs. Respective field를 정할 수 있음. Embedding of node를 결정. 많이 겹칠수록 embedding이 비슷해짐. 많이 stacking할수록 겹치는 부분이 많아져서 over-smoothing 문제. Shallow GNN로 더 expressive하게 하기 위해서는 expressive power within each GNN layer를 늘려야 함. ⇒ Message & aggregation function을 deep neural network로 구성. GNN layer 전후로 MLP layer를 넣을 수 있음. 그럼에도 GNN layer가 많이 필요하다면…? Skip connections Earlier GNN layer가 더 좋을 수도 있음. ⇒ Add shortcut.

Handling sparse graphs

⇒ Add virtual nodes or edges. ① Adding virtual edges: connect 2-hop neighbors via virtual edges.

A←A+A2(adjacency matrix).A\leftarrow A+A^2\quad\text{(adjacency matrix)}.A←A+A2(adjacency matrix).

② Adding virtual nodes: which is connected to all nodes. ⇒ Shortest distance가 2가 됨. ⇒ Message processing procedure가 효율적이게 됨.

Handling dense graphs

Message passing is too costly. ⇒ Sample neighbors in the message passing process.

Ch. 8 Knowledge Graph Embedding

Triplet (head entity, relation, tail entity). Knowledge graph G=(V,R,E)G=(V,R,E)G=(V,R,E): VVV entities, RRR relations, EEE triplets. Head나 tail을 예측. Knowledge graph embedding: represent the entities and relations in a low-dimensional feature space. 단계:

  1. Represent entities & relations.
  2. Define a scoring function fr(h,t)f_r(h,t)fr​(h,t) ← plausibility 측정 (타당성).
  3. Learn entity and relation representations.

Translational distance model: use distance-based scoring function. Ex. TransE, TransH, TransR, RotatE. Semantic matching model: exploit similarity-based scoring function. Ex. RESCAL, DistMult, HolE.

Negative sampling

Generating negative training examples. Negative sample을 만들기 위해 hhh나 ttt를 임의로 교체. 이 때 교체했을 때 sample이 positive일 확률을 negative sample로 조정. 1:N이면 head를, N:1이면 tail을 더 교체해서 false negative sample 생성 방지 가능. Self-adversarial negative sampling in RotatE Sample negative triplets according to the current embedding model. Learn entity and relation representations θ\thetaθ by minimizing the pairwise ranking loss.

알고리즘

Knowledge graph embedding with GNNs

Relational GCN (RGCN)

Average info from nbrs and apply a neural network. 만약 relation type이 다르면 각각 다른 neural network weight 적용. Add reversed relations for message passing. Each relation has LLL matrices: Wr(1),…,Wr(L)W_r^{(1)},\ldots,W_r^{(L)}Wr(1)​,…,Wr(L)​. Size of Wr(ℓ)W_r^{(\ell)}Wr(ℓ)​ = d(ℓ+1)×d(ℓ)d^{(\ell+1)}\times d^{(\ell)}d(ℓ+1)×d(ℓ) ← hidden dimension in layer ℓ\ellℓ. Relation이 많아지면 parameter수가 급격히 많아짐. Regularize the weights Wr(ℓ)W_r^{(\ell)}Wr(ℓ)​: ① Block-diagonal decomposition, ② Basis decomposition. ① Block-diagonal decomposition ⇒ make the weights sparse.

d(ℓ+1)×d(ℓ)→B×d(ℓ+1)B×d(ℓ)B.d^{(\ell+1)}\times d^{(\ell)}\quad\to\quad B\times\frac{d^{(\ell+1)}}B\times\frac{d^{(\ell)}}B.d(ℓ+1)×d(ℓ)→B×Bd(ℓ+1)​×Bd(ℓ)​.

② Basis decomposition ⇒ share weights across different relations. Matrix of each relation as a linear combination of basis transformations.

Wr=∑b=1BarbVb.W_r=\sum_{b=1}^Ba_{rb}V_b.Wr​=b=1∑B​arb​Vb​.

VbV_bVb​: BBB basis matrices, shared across all relations. arba_{rb}arb​: importance weight of matrix VbV_bVb​. ⇒ {arb}b=1B\{a_{rb}\}_{b=1}^B{arb​}b=1B​만 학습하면 됨.

Link prediction

RGCN: encoder, DistMult: decoder. ∀r\forall r∀r is associated with a diagonal matrix RrR_rRr​ (d×dd\times dd×d). (E,r3,A)(E,r_3,A)(E,r3​,A): supervision triplet 가정 (감독). hE(L),hA(L)h_E^{(L)},h_A^{(L)}hE(L)​,hA(L)​을 통해 score function 계산. DistMult:

fr3(hE,hA)=hETWr3hA.f_{r_3}(h_E,h_A)=h_E^TW_{r_3}h_A.fr3​​(hE​,hA​)=hET​Wr3​​hA​.

Training

  1. (E,r3,A)(E,r_3,A)(E,r3​,A): training supervision triplet 가정.
  2. Negative sampling (≠\ne= training triplet).
  3. RGCN → represent node embedding.
  4. DistMult → represent relations. Optimize margin-based ranking loss.

Evaluation Predict validation of (E,r3,D)(E,r_3,D)(E,r3​,D). Score should be higher than (E,r3,v)(E,r_3,v)(E,r3​,v), ∀v\forall v∀v where (E,r3,v)(E,r_3,v)(E,r3​,v) is not in training triplets. ⇒ Obtain ranking of (E,r3,D)(E,r_3,D)(E,r3​,D) → calculate metrics. Ex. MR, MRR, Hit @ n.

Evaluation & applications

Benchmark dataset

  • Freebase: community members에 의해서 자유롭게 만들어짐.
  • NELL (Never-Ending Language Learning): semantic relation.
  • WordNet: lexical DB of semantic relations.

Data splitting

  1. Train set: optimize model parameters, learn the embeddings.
  2. Validation set: used for tuning hyperparameters.
  3. Test set: used for testing performance.

Link prediction:

  • Entity prediction: (?,r,t)(?,r,t)(?,r,t), (h,r,?)(h,r,?)(h,r,?).
  • Relation prediction: (h,?,t)(h,?,t)(h,?,t).

(?,r,t)(?,r,t)(?,r,t)에서 그냥 모든 hhh에 대해 score 구하고 ranking으로 예측 가능. TransE를 사용해서 embedding을 학습한다면,

fr(h,t)=−∥h+r−t∥.f_r(h,t)=-\|h+r-t\|.fr​(h,t)=−∥h+r−t∥.

Evaluation할 때 (h,r,t)∈test set(h,r,t)\in\text{test set}(h,r,t)∈test set. ⇒ Make (?,r,t)(?,r,t)(?,r,t), (h,r,?)(h,r,?)(h,r,?) problems. ⇒ Score ranking. ⇒ Record ranks of correct answers in the ordered lists.

  1. Mean Rank (MR) → 평균 랭킹 계산, lower the better.
  2. Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) → 역수 랭킹 평균 계산, higher better.
  3. Hit @ N → proportion of ranks no larger than NNN, higher better.

MR vs MRR: MR은 랭킹이 많이 바뀔 때, MRR은 top-ranked가 바뀔 때 많이 바뀜. With filtered metrics: some problem has many solutions. 다른 정답인 애들을 빼고 랭킹 고려.

Recommender system

User의 rating 예측 (추천). Collaborative filtering: 사용자로부터 정보 수집. Matrix factorization

R≈UMT,Rij≈uiTmj.R\approx UM^T,\qquad R_{ij}\approx u_i^Tm_j.R≈UMT,Rij​≈uiT​mj​.

Col of UUU: latent (잠재의) factors for users. Col of MMM: latent factors for movies. Row iii of UUU: user iii's low-dim representation. Row jjj of MMM: movie jjj's low-dim representation. How to find ui,mju_i,m_jui​,mj​?

min⁡u1,…,um, m1,…,mn∑(i,j)∈S(Rij−uiTmj)2+λ∑i∥ui∥22+λ∑j∥mj∥22\min_{u_1,\ldots,u_m,\,m_1,\ldots,m_n}\sum_{(i,j)\in S}(R_{ij}-u_i^Tm_j)^2 +\lambda\sum_i\|u_i\|_2^2+\lambda\sum_j\|m_j\|_2^2u1​,…,um​,m1​,…,mn​min​(i,j)∈S∑​(Rij​−uiT​mj​)2+λi∑​∥ui​∥22​+λj∑​∥mj​∥22​

≡∥W⊙(R−UMT)∥F2+λ(∥U∥F2+∥M∥F2).\equiv\|W\odot(R-UM^T)\|_F^2+\lambda(\|U\|_F^2+\|M\|_F^2).≡∥W⊙(R−UMT)∥F2​+λ(∥U∥F2​+∥M∥F2​).

Wij=1W_{ij}=1Wij​=1 if (i,j)∈S(i,j)\in S(i,j)∈S (known rating), otherwise 0. ⊙\odot⊙: elementwise product. Alternating minimization: fix UUU and compute MMM, then fix MMM and compute UUU, …반복. When we fix MMM, RT≈MUTR^T\approx MU^TRT≈MUT. 이것과 다음 문제 번갈아 푸는구나 → missing value 무시.

min⁡u1,…,um∑i=1m∥ri−Mui∥22+λ∑i=1m∥ui∥22: Ridge Regression.\min_{u_1,\ldots,u_m}\sum_{i=1}^m\|r_i-Mu_i\|_2^2+\lambda\sum_{i=1}^m\|u_i\|_2^2 \quad\text{: Ridge Regression}.u1​,…,um​min​i=1∑m​∥ri​−Mui​∥22​+λi=1∑m​∥ui​∥22​: Ridge Regression.

Preference of user iii to item jjj ⇒ uiTmju_i^Tm_juiT​mj​. Ranking optimization over pairwise preference ⇒ used to learn latent vectors.
